thread:
maya: FYI — multiple teams are asking for quick SIEM exports to triage vulnerabilities. We need a hardened, repeatable JIT extract flow (RBAC + KMS + DLP) that product can use without opening keys. Thoughts? :mag:

elena: Absolutely. We should standardize: ticket -> minimal fields checklist -> automated DLP scan -> approver -> ephemeral RBAC + KMS-proxy unwrap -> export into secured bucket with short TTL.

carter: Important: the IAM temp role should never include raw kms:Decrypt. Instead, the role allows calling a proxy endpoint that performs the unwrap and returns an ephemeral artifact tied to ticket, expiry, and consumer host.

simon: Auditability: every proxy call emits an immutable record to the audit-index. Fields: ticket_id, requester, approver, source_path, dest_bucket, object_sha256, dlp_result, unwrap_token_id. That index is WORM and access-limited.

maya: Can we define the ticket minimums so approvers don't have to guess?

elena: Proposed ticket template snippet to copy into ops: 

```
Type: JIT-SIEM-EXPORT
Requester: <okta_id>
Ticket: INC-<num>
Purpose: <one-line>
Scope: explicit index paths / query / time range
Fields: CSV list (no wildcard)
PII? yes/no -> if yes list 1-2 fields allowed
Retention requested: 30d (default) / up to 365d (legal signoff req)
Deliverable: masked-csv | secure-s3-link
Approver: SOC lead
```

carter: Automation for RBAC: label the IAM request with ticket=INC-###. The grant workflow will mint a short-lived binding in the identity service for 2-6 hours. Longer than 8h => manual escalation to SOC manager + legal.

oncall: Approver UX: SOC lead receives a compact DM with quick facts + Approve / Deny buttons. Approve triggers the KMS-proxy grant and posts an audit event. Deny sends template explaining next steps.

infra-bot: "audit:event created: export.requested ticket=INC-30102 requester=maya status=awaiting_approval"

simon: Pre-export checks: run DLP regexes (aws secrets, private keys, bearer tokens), run sensitive-field whitelist/blacklist, and compute object checksum. If DLP fails -> block and notify security. Callout: add a second owner to review if export contains >5k rows of potentially sensitive PII.

maya: Implementation detail for KMS proxy: proxy returns an ephemeral URL or single-use token that only the export process can use. No key material escapes. Token metadata includes ticket and expiry and is logged. Example call: 

```
POST /kms-proxy/unlock
{ "ticket": "INC-30102", "object_path": "s3://secure/exports/INC-30102/part-000.csv" }
Response: { "ephemeral_token": "tok_abc123", "expires_at": "2026-03-25T15:00Z" }
```

elena: DLP command we run in CI / preflight: `tools/dlp_scan --file /tmp/export.csv --rules dlp/default.json`. Exit code != 0 => fail. We should surface the rule hits in the ticket so approver can see exactly which patterns matched.

carter: Storage & TTL: default export bucket has lifecycle rule to delete objects after 30d. For evidence retention >30d we require evidence justification + legal approval; such exports are moved to a gated bucket and object retention set to requested days up to 365.

legal: Quick note: any export containing EU personal data must specify region and retention explicitly. Legal needs the ticket id and justification to sign off. Also prefer hashed identifiers where possible.

maya: How do we prevent accidental mass exports?
simon: Enforce row & field caps in the exporter. Default max rows = 50k. Any request for more must include business justification in ticket and go through manual review. Also require explicit field-level affirmation (checkbox) in UI to confirm PII handling.

elena: Forensics chain: exporter writes a manifest: { ticket, manifest_ts, src_query, dest_path, object_sha256, dlp_summary }. The manifest is stored in the audit bucket and cross-linked in the ticket.

infra-bot: "stored manifest: s3://audit/manifests/INC-30102-manifest.json (encrypted)"

oncall: Tests: add an integration test in infra-ci that simulates: create ticket -> mock approve -> call kms-proxy -> run dlp scan (include both pass and fail fixtures) -> verify audit events and lifecycle rules run. Assign owner?

carter: I'll own the test and the IAM automation hook. I'll put a draft PR by Thursday.

elena: I'll draft the runbook and include the ticket template, approver checklist, sample DM payload, DLP rule links, and manifests example.

maya: Great. Final checklist for runbook: exact RBAC bindings, KMS-proxy API spec, DLP command/examples, default retention + escalation path, audit fields and access list, and CI test path. Can someone call out escalation contacts in the doc?

simon: SOC lead + oncall + legal. I'll add exact aliases.

maya: Thanks — once we have PRs let's schedule a 30-min tabletop with SOC and product security to run a simulated request. Want to ensure approvals are quick but safe. :shield:
